name: The old prophet of Beth-el
charge: Lying in the name of the Lord, claiming an angel’s word, to turn a prophet from his charge
summary: An old prophet living in Bethel heard from his sons what the man of God from Judah had done at Jeroboam’s altar, rode after him, and brought him back to eat and drink by claiming that an angel had spoken to him by the word of the Lord; but he lied to him (1 Kings 13:11-19). At the table the true word came through the liar himself, the man of God was killed by a lion on the road, and the old prophet buried him in his own grave and asked to be laid beside him, confessing that the word against Bethel would surely come to pass (1 Kings 13:20-32). No sentence on the old prophet is recorded.
offenseFull: The man of God had kept his charge before the king: no bread, no water, and home by another way (1 Kings 13:7-10). Then there dwelt an old prophet in Bethel, the city of Jeroboam’s calf. His sons told him all the works the man of God had done and the words he had spoken to the king, and showed him which way he had gone. He had them saddle the ass, rode after him, and found him sitting under an oak, and asked whether he was the man of God who came from Judah (1 Kings 13:11-14). He invited him home to eat bread. The man of God repeated the word of the Lord to him: he could not return, go in, eat or drink in that place (1 Kings 13:15-17). The old man answered that he was a prophet also, and an angel had spoken to him by the word of the Lord to bring him back to eat bread and drink water; but he lied to him (1 Kings 13:18). So the man of God went back with him and ate (1 Kings 13:19).

The teaching hears the voice of the serpent with Eve: first a little resistance, then the voice that talks a man out of a plain command. He came with a claim no one could check, an angel’s word, but the Lord speaks to His prophets in visions and dreams and mouth to mouth only with Moses (Numbers 12:6-8); this man said an angel came to him, and he was lying. A prophet who presumes to speak a word in the name of the Lord which He has not commanded him to speak is condemned by the law (Deuteronomy 18:20). When a student asked in class who the old prophet was, the answer was that the moral is not who he was but what he did to the man of God: he made

himself equal to him, so the man let his guard down. That is why the congregation does not hook up with every other camp that quotes the same scriptures and claims the Lord is working with them too, for such a man will get you killed. The class note sets it beside Jeremiah’s warning not to put blind trust in a brother, because brothers supplant one another (Jeremiah 9:4).
judgmentFull: The word of the Lord came to the old prophet at his own table, and he had to cry out the sentence on the man he had deceived: because he disobeyed the Lord’s command, his body would not be buried in the tomb of his fathers (1 Kings 13:20-22). A lion killed the man of God on the road and stood by the body with the ass, and when men told it in the city, the old prophet said it was the man of God who had been disobedient to the word of the Lord (1 Kings 13:23-26). The study notes say the Most High used the deceiver to prove whether the man would keep his charge, for the deceived and the deceiver are His (Job 12:16).

He went, found the body untouched, brought it back on the ass, laid it in his own grave, and mourned over him as his brother. He told his sons that when he died they should bury him in the same sepulchre and lay his bones beside the bones of the man of God, for the word cried against the altar in Bethel and against the high places of Samaria would surely come to pass (1 Kings 13:27-32). History in the AM notes the point for Jeroboam: the Lord had shown him that the word was real, first by the sign on the altar and then by the death of the man who disobeyed it. Scripture records no punishment for the old prophet. What it records is that his confession came true. Josiah burned the bones of Bethel on its altar, and when he came to the tomb of the man of God he said to let him alone; so they let his bones alone, together with the bones of the prophet who had asked to lie beside him (2 Kings 23:17-18).

text.text: Now there dwelt an old prophet in Beth–el; and his sons came and told him all the works that the man of God had done that day in Beth–el: the words which he had spoken unto the king, them they told also to their father.
And their father said unto them, What way went he? For his sons had seen what way the man of God went, which came from Judah.
And he said unto his sons, Saddle me the ass. So they saddled him the ass: and he rode thereon,
And went after the man of God, and found him sitting under an oak: and he said unto him, Art thou the man of God that camest from Judah? And he said, I am.
Then he said unto him, Come home with me, and eat bread.
And he said, I may not return with thee, nor go in with thee: neither will I eat bread nor drink water with thee in this place:
For it was said to me by the word of the Lord, Thou shalt eat no bread nor drink water there, nor turn again to go by the way that thou camest.

He said unto him, I am a prophet also as thou art; and an angel spake unto me by the word of the Lord, saying, Bring him back with thee into thine house, that he may eat bread and drink water. But he lied unto him.
So he went back with him, and did eat bread in his house, and drank water.
And it came to pass, as they sat at the table, that the word of the Lord came unto the prophet that brought him back:

And he cried unto the man of God that came from Judah, saying, Thus saith the Lord, Forasmuch as thou hast disobeyed the mouth of the Lord, and hast not kept the commandment which the Lord thy God commanded thee,

But camest back, and hast eaten bread and drunk water in the place, of the which the Lord did say to thee, Eat no bread, and drink no water; thy carcase shall not come unto the sepulchre of thy fathers.
And it came to pass, after he had eaten bread, and after he had drunk, that he saddled for him the ass, to wit, for the prophet whom he had brought back.
And when he was gone, a lion met him by the way, and slew him: and his carcase was cast in the way, and the ass stood by it, the lion also stood by the carcase.
And, behold, men passed by, and saw the carcase cast in the way, and the lion standing by the carcase: and they came and told it in the city where the old prophet dwelt.

And when the prophet that brought him back from the way heard thereof, he said, It is the man of God, who was disobedient unto the word of the Lord: therefore the Lord hath delivered him unto the lion, which hath torn him, and slain him, according to the word of the Lord, which he spake unto him.
And he spake to his sons, saying, Saddle me the ass. And they saddled him.
And he went and found his carcase cast in the way, and the ass and the lion standing by the carcase: the lion had not eaten the carcase, nor torn the ass.
And the prophet took up the carcase of the man of God, and laid it upon the ass, and brought it back: and the old prophet came to the city, to mourn and to bury him.
And he laid his carcase in his own grave; and they mourned over him, saying, Alas, my brother!
And it came to pass, after he had buried him, that he spake to his sons, saying, When I am dead, then bury me in the sepulchre wherein the man of God is buried; lay my bones beside his bones:
For the saying which he cried by the word of the Lord against the altar in Beth–el, and against all the houses of the high places which are in the cities of Samaria, shall surely come to pass.
And the king said unto the man of God, Come home with me, and refresh thyself, and I will give thee a reward.
And the man of God said unto the king, If thou wilt give me half thine house, I will not go in with thee, neither will I eat bread nor drink water in this place:
For so was it charged me by the word of the Lord, saying, Eat no bread, nor drink water, nor turn again by the same way that thou camest.
So he went another way, and returned not by the way that he came to Beth–el.

Now there dwelt an old prophet in Beth–el; and his sons came and told him all the works that the man of God had done that day in Beth–el: the words which he had spoken unto the king, them they told also to their father.
And their father said unto them, What way went he? For his sons had seen what way the man of God went, which came from Judah.
And he said unto his sons, Saddle me the ass. So they saddled him the ass: and he rode thereon,
And went after the man of God, and found him sitting under an oak: and he said unto him, Art thou the man of God that camest from Judah? And he said, I am.
Then he said unto him, Come home with me, and eat bread.
And he said, I may not return with thee, nor go in with thee: neither will I eat bread nor drink water with thee in this place:
For it was said to me by the word of the Lord, Thou shalt eat no bread nor drink water there, nor turn again to go by the way that thou camest.

He said unto him, I am a prophet also as thou art; and an angel spake unto me by the word of the Lord, saying, Bring him back with thee into thine house, that he may eat bread and drink water. But he lied unto him.
So he went back with him, and did eat bread in his house, and drank water.
And he said, Hear now my words: If there be a prophet among you, I the Lord will make myself known unto him in a vision, and will speak unto him in a dream.
My servant Moses is not so, who is faithful in all mine house.
With him will I speak mouth to mouth, even apparently, and not in dark speeches; and the similitude of the Lord shall he behold: wherefore then were ye not afraid to speak against my servant Moses?
But the prophet, which shall presume to speak a word in my name, which I have not commanded him to speak, or that shall speak in the name of other gods, even that prophet shall die.
Take ye heed every one of his neighbour, and trust ye not in any brother: for every brother will utterly supplant, and every neighbour will walk with slanders.
